# Hugh Carrow

## Appearance

Hugh is a tall, high-statured youth with broad shoulders, wavy chestnut hair, and bright, direct, mischievous light-brown or hazel eyes. He is exceptionally good-looking and manly, with a mouth that often curls into a mocking or admiring grin. After a winter of intense study at college, he appeared temporarily pale and thin.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P32](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0032), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c37 P37](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0037), [v2 c19 P50](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0050), [v3 c5 P1](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0001), [v3 c39 P22](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0022)_

## Personality

Hugh is intelligent, studious, and ambitious, possessing individual perspectives and a drive to extract the finest elements from life while contributing his utmost. He has a playful, mischievous side and a keen appreciation for humor, often teasing schoolmates with jokes and pranks. In his relationships, he is generous, considerate, and deeply devoted, holding high moral principles and exercising careful self-discipline. As a physician, he is deeply principled and willing to take risks to preserve patient life and health.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v1 c38 P38](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0038), [v2 c19 P51](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0051), [v3 c27 P36](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0036), [v4 c29 P16](../source/v04-c29.md#nw-v04-c29-p0016)_

## History

Hugh spent three years in Alberta with his ill father before returning to Brierley, where he entered school and quickly became Nell Harcourt's primary academic competitor. Despite early friction caused by his teasing, he developed deep feelings for Nell and retrieved a rose she dropped. When both sought the local teaching position, Hugh generously withdrew his application in favor of Nell's and taught at Pale Sands instead to fund his future college education. He organized and served as president of the Brierley Village Improvement Society and co-wrote newspaper notes under the pen name 'Observer'. At Regent's Academy, he won the class medal, and subsequently attended Wexcombe College alongside Nell, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the Arts Rush, was elected Freshman Class President, served as football captain, and joined the Lambs society. Although Nell initially rejected his declaration of love, Hugh remained a steady friend while working rigorously to achieve High Honors in Classics and win the Cooper Prize. Near the end of his college years, he fell severely ill with typhoid fever; during his recovery, he and Nell realized their mutual love and became betrothed. Following three years of medical studies, Hugh married Nell in the orchard at Grey Shutters. He subsequently relocated with her to Glen St. Agnes to take over the medical practice of his great-uncle, Dr. David Carrow.

## Quotes

> I believe Portmaris will suit us. People say it’s a pleasant old town, complete with the most splendid natural park anywhere. The landscape there is supposed to be grand, from what I’ve been told.  <sub>[v3 c1 P22](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0022)</sub>

> However, Nell, you must be prepared for a lengthy wait. Three years will pass before my studies in medicine are complete. Furthermore, even at that point, marble halls and diamond sunbursts will not be ours.  <sub>[v3 c41 P36](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0036)</sub>

> Nell, I have given exhaustive thought to that side of the matter. However, it is my belief that a physician must place the holiness of a patient's mind and body higher than any other concerns, regardless of the repercussions. It is my conviction that his obligation is to strive to bring back health and sanity, provided any prospect at all remains.  <sub>[v4 c29 P16](../source/v04-c29.md#nw-v04-c29-p0016)</sub>

> If I had hesitated to perform a particular test, Rhoda Allonby would not be among the living now. I accepted the danger—and rescued her.  <sub>[v4 c29 P22](../source/v04-c29.md#nw-v04-c29-p0022)</sub>

> I shall call Uncle Dave on the telephone,  <sub>[v4 c31 P22](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0022)</sub>
